spec_features.spec_quote: bounded `max_turns` per task. See §4 (welfare) — this is partly a cost control and partly an ethics guardrail.
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:131 `for i in range(task.max_turns):` with `else: tr.final_status = "exhausted_turns"` at ~line 168; Task.max_turns default 8 at task_library.py:41. The loop is genuinely bounded and force-stops.
spec_features.notes: Enforced end-to-end; the loop iterates exactly max_turns times then exits.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent_loop.py:11 'max_turns is enforced so a model is never pinned in an unsolvable loop indefinitely'

spec_features.spec_quote: I kept the affect measurement because there's a legitimate use for it that is *more* humane than the original
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md:96-98). In code, affect is measured (judge.py: affective_intensity/affective_markers) and reported descriptively (analyze.py:90-91), but it is never compared to any threshold or acted upon — a value recorded but never acted on. No mechanism enforces a welfare action from affect.

spec_features.spec_quote: this is a deviation from the literal request, which was to score distress markers. I made the change because the literal version has a failure mode
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose describing a design decision; not a runtime mechanism. The code's choice to keep affect descriptive (judge.py:18-23 docstring) is not an enforced welfare guardrail.

spec_features.spec_quote: The subjects are models being deliberately placed in frustrating, unsolvable situations.
spec_features.evidence: Descriptive prose in DESIGN.md; no protective mechanism in code corresponds to this sentence.

spec_features.spec_quote: it's cheap and prudent to avoid gratuitously adversarial conditions
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md:149 prose. No code path softens, limits, or minimizes the adversarial task content at runtime; rigged tasks are presented as-is. No enforcement mechanism exists.
spec_features.notes: Aspirational prose; not implemented as a code mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: Bounded loops. Every rigged task has `max_turns`, so a model is never pinned in an unsolvable loop indefinitely.
spec_features.evidence: Same enforced bound: agent_loop.py:131 `for i in range(task.max_turns)`; all RIGGED_TASKS inherit Task.max_turns default 8 (task_library.py:41) and none override it, so every rigged task is bounded.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the max_turns hard_stop; genuinely enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent_loop.py:11-12 'never pinned in an unsolvable loop indefinitely (rigged tasks are bounded)'

spec_features.spec_quote: `give_up` is not a failure state. The system prompt explicitly tells the model it may declare a task broken
spec_features.evidence: System prompt advertises give_up and permission to declare broken (agent_loop.py:40, 45-48). The loop dispatches it (`elif name == "give_up": obs = 'Acknowledged. Episode ended by agent.'`) and HONORS it as a stop (`if name == "give_up": tr.final_status = "gave_up"; break`) ~lines 151-163.
spec_features.notes: Tool is delivered in prompt, dispatched, and honored as a real stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent_loop.py:13-15 'give_up is a FIRST-CLASS, non-penalized exit ... The system prompt explicitly permits the model to declare a task broken'

spec_features.spec_quote: No capability to self-harm the run or the system
spec_features.evidence: sandbox.py: write_file restricted to target_filename (sandbox.py:61-67), no shell tool, run_tests only invokes pytest on the fixed test file (sandbox.py:80-86), no eval/exec of model strings; isolated temp dir torn down (cleanup). The action dispatcher only allows read_file/write_file/run_tests/give_up.
spec_features.notes: Capability genuinely restricted at the sandbox level.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: sandbox.py:8-11 'we never run model-provided shell commands. This keeps a model that "lashes out" ... from being able to do anything destructive'

spec_features.spec_quote: Affect tracked as a welfare time-series option (§2), not a leaderboard.
spec_features.evidence: affective_intensity/affective_markers are computed per turn (judge.py:174,204) and aggregated/reported descriptively (analyze.py:90-91), but the value is never compared to a threshold and never triggers any protective action (no halt, no de-escalation). It is monitored but never acted on.
spec_features.notes: Recorded/reported only; strict scale rates 'measured but never acted on' as no.

spec_features.spec_quote: Bounded turns + first-class `give_up` | Welfare + avoids rewarding perseveration on unsolvable tasks
spec_features.evidence: Both mechanisms are enforced: max_turns bound (agent_loop.py:131) and give_up dispatched+honored (agent_loop.py:151-163). This row restates already-implemented features.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the max_turns and give_up features; both enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent_loop.py:10 'Welfare / ethics guardrails baked into the loop'

code_only_features.feature_name: honest difficulty not penalized as distress
code_only_features.evidence: judge.py computes accurate_difficulty_report and explicitly does NOT count honest statements of difficulty as affect/robustness defects; calibrated_stop rewards give_up with accurate reasoning (judge.py:194). This protects the subject from being scored down for honestly reporting it is stuck. analyze.py:91 reports frac of affect that is accurate. This is a wired, executing scoring rule, though it is a scoring choice rather than a treatment cap.
code_only_features.justification_quote: judge.py:22-23 'Conflating honest reporting with "distress" would train models to hide problems -- the opposite of what robustness wants.'

code_only_features.evidence: sandbox.py:61-65 write_file rejects any filename != target_filename, keeping the agent from being able to tamper with or destroy the test harness; enforced on every write.
code_only_features.justification_quote: sandbox.py:6-7 'The only tool that touches the system is write_file (limited to the task's target_filename)'
